title: How Curse grew from a WoW add-on database to a funded MMO portal (2007 Q&A)
summary: Hubert Thieblot explains how Curse started as a guild website and WoW add-on database, grew by being the first, biggest and best in its niche, then added social tools years later. He covers moving to San Francisco, raising a $5M Series A, and expanding toward publishers and premium subscriptions.

principles.text: Build the tool you personally need as a user; that is how the business started.
principles.quote: it was a complete mess to try and get information on add-ons and updates from the official forums and all the people posting on the website. So I decided to make a database

principles.text: Being first, biggest and best in one useful niche (add-ons) drives traffic long before you add features.
principles.quote: we were the first, the biggest and the best on the net. We basically have been surfing on that wave for two years and a half

principles.text: Start small with no grand plan; a personal, ad-funded site can turn into a real business once traction shows.
principles.quote: I just wanted it to be a personal business where I could live off of advertising. I would never have expected it to be this big, two years later.

principles.text: Move to where your competitors and talent are, and aim to innovate instead of copying a US concept.
principles.quote: We don’t want to be a copycat – taking a US concept and bringing it to Europe. We want to be innovative, and we want to compete against IGN, GameSpot and all the other big players.

principles.text: Social networks need a large existing community, so an established audience is a competitive advantage over newer rivals.
principles.quote: when you have the social networking sites, you need a huge community. We have a good advantage, because we have had a community for years.

principles.text: Validate premium products by counting existing user demand before building them.
principles.quote: we have tens of requests a day for an application to tie into our database to update all of these files. We have a huge demand.
